newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Mystery pooch poisoner kills 61 Hong Kong dogs.
newsitem.headline: Mystery pooch poisoner kills 61 Hong Kong dogs.

text.p: A mystery poisoner has killed at least 61 dogs in Hong Kong's trendy Mid-Levels residential district, vets were quoted on Thursday as saying.
The figures came from eight vets who treated dogs taken ill after walking in the popular area, home to many of Hong Kong's expatriates, the South China Morning Post said.
An earlier report this week said one of the dogs which had a close brush with death but survived was colonial Governor Chris Patten's Norfolk Terrier named Whisky.
One of the not-so-lucky victims that died was a Jack Russell called Rocky, a canine celebrity which had starred in adverts for the territory's top-class Conrad Hotel.
"The vet said the poison was strong enough to kill a small child," said Rocky's owner Roger Patterson.
Vets said the death toll could actually be much higher. The cases, in which dogs eat poison-laced food left on the ground, began three to four years ago, the vets said.
Police said they have other priorities and that it will be hard to catch the serial pooch killer without a helpful tip-off.
